name: Musakhan (Sumac Chicken and Caramelized Onions)
writer_notes: SELECTOR: Roast chicken over deeply caramelized onions on flatbread; pita-bread is a tracked commodity so the base is board-mapped, and onions are one of the cheapest board items, which makes this a genuinely low cost-per-serving entry. Sumac is the signature spice and has no board home - flagged, not hidden. Pine nuts optional, almonds tracked as a swap. Confidence: MEDIUM - URL confirmed on site search index, page not individually fetched. | HARVEST: No nutrition box published. Source sections: For Spice Mixture (6 lines), For Chicken (5), For Flatbread (8). The spice mixture makes more than the recipe uses.
OVERRIDE Tortilla: '6 flatbread (taboon/pita/naan)' - naan-size flatbread is ~90 g, not a 30 g tortilla
OVERRIDE Ground Allspice: WAVE-5: source '3 tbsp allspice' at sauce-tbsp default weight blew up to 134 g/batch; sumac leads musakhan, allspice supports - 1 tbsp at source scale (~17 g/batch)
OVERRIDE Salt: AUDIT B3: two unquantified 'Kosher salt' lines each drew the 20 g house staple -> 117 g/batch; clamped to the single house TO_TASTE level (~20 g/batch)
intro_html: Musakhan is Palestine's national dish and it is built on two things almost nobody in an American kitchen thinks of as a main event: onions and bread. Pounds of onions cook down slowly in olive oil until they are soft and sweet, sumac turns them a dusty red and makes them taste like lemon without any lemon in the pot, and it all goes over flatbread that soaks up everything. Roast chicken sits on top. Each portion runs 576 calories and 42 grams of protein for about $4.48 (at everyday cost).
ingredients_display: Boneless Skinless Chicken Thigh (Member's Mark): 3.75 lb (1750 g)
cost_note_html: Real Omaha store prices from our weekly grocery board (2026). They still swing by store and by what is on sale.
cost_lines: Boneless Skinless Chicken Thigh, 3.75 lb: ~$6.83. Buy 4 lbs: $7.08.
Pantry seasonings (ground allspice, ground cinnamon, black pepper, garam masala, ground nutmeg, salt, ground cumin): ~$2.59. From jars you keep on hand.

Batch total: about $24.95 across 14 servings, so roughly $1.78 per bowl. This counts only the amounts this batch actually uses from each package, so it is the cost of the food in the containers, not a register receipt.

True shopping cost: about $28.16 across 14 servings, roughly $2.01 per bowl. What the register trip looks like if your pantry is already stocked. Meat, produce, and packaged items are counted as the whole packages you have to buy, since you cannot grab a partial box, can, or jar. Pantry staples you already own (rice, seasonings, oils, and long-lasting sauces) are counted at only what this batch uses.

Starting with an empty pantry? Add about $28.78 one time. That is the extra cost of buying full containers of every pantry staple in this recipe instead of just the amounts used, which puts a first shopping trip near $56.94. Those containers then feed this batch and many more after it.
cost_closing_html: About $4.48 a portion (at everyday cost). The flatbread and the onions together cost more than the chicken does, which tells you exactly what kind of dish this is: one that was designed to make a little meat feed a lot of people.
shop_smart: You need a serious quantity of onions, so buy the five pound bag. The per-pound price on a big bag runs a fraction of the loose bin and onions keep for a month in a dry cabinet.

Sumac is the one spice with no substitute here, since it is what makes musakhan taste like musakhan. Buy it from a Middle Eastern grocer where it costs a third of what the gourmet spice shops charge, and one bag lasts a very long time.
Flatbread is the biggest single line. Buy the large packs of the cheapest soft flatbread your store sells, since it is going under a pile of hot onions and nobody will notice the brand.
Olive oil belongs in this dish and there is no getting around it, but you do not need extra virgin for cooking onions down for half an hour. Buy the big jug of regular olive oil for this one.
make_it: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Slice all the onions thin. This is the longest part of the recipe and there is no way around it, so put on something to listen to and get it done.

Toss the chicken thighs with some of the olive oil, salt, black pepper, ground allspice, ground cinnamon, ground cumin, garam masala, ground nutmeg and a generous spoonful of the sumac. Let them sit while the oven heats to 425F.

Cook the sliced onions in the rest of the olive oil in your largest pot over medium-low heat for 30 to 40 minutes, stirring occasionally, until they collapse into a soft sweet jam. Low and slow. If they are browning fast, the heat is too high.
Stir the bulk of the sumac into the cooked onions and let it cook another 5 minutes until they turn deep red and smell tart.
Roast the seasoned chicken on a sheet pan for 25 to 30 minutes, until it reads 165F and the edges are dark. Save every drop of the pan drippings.
Warm the tortillas, tear them into large pieces, and toss them in your mixing pot with the pan drippings so they soak up the fat rather than staying dry.
Chop the chicken, fold it together with the sumac onions and the soaked bread, and finish with the chopped cilantro.
portion_html: Set the pot on the scale, subtract the empty-pot weight, and divide by 14. Fourteen equal containers. Each one carries 576 calories, and the bread softens as it sits, which is not a flaw here, it is the entire idea behind the dish.

head.keywords: musakhan, sumac chicken, palestinian chicken, caramelized onion chicken, middle eastern meal prep, flatbread chicken
recipeIngredient: Ground allspice, ground cinnamon, ground cumin, garam masala and ground nutmeg
steps: Season the chicken thighs with olive oil, sumac, allspice, cinnamon, cumin, garam masala and nutmeg.
Cook the thinly sliced onions in olive oil over medium-low heat for 30 to 40 minutes until jammy.
Stir the remaining sumac into the onions and cook 5 more minutes.
Roast the chicken at 425F for 25 to 30 minutes until it reads 165F, saving the drippings.
Toss torn warm tortillas in the drippings, fold with the onions and chopped chicken, and portion into 14 containers.
